claim: Many classes of drugs can induce fatal cardiac arrhythmias by disrupting the electrophysiology of cardiomyocytes.
source: Many classes of drugs can induce fatal cardiac arrhythmias by disrupting the electrophysiology of cardiomyocytes.
evidence: This is a general statement about drug-induced arrhythmias that is supported by established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: Safety guidelines require all new drugs to be assessed for pro-arrhythmic risk prior to conducting human trials.
source: Safety guidelines thus require all new drugs to be assessed for pro-arrhythmic risk prior to conducting human trials.
evidence: This refers to established regulatory requirements in drug development.

claim: Standard safety protocols primarily focus on drug blockade of the delayed-rectifier potassium current (IKr).
source: The standard safety protocols primarily focus on drug blockade of the delayed-rectifier potassium current (IKr).
evidence: This is supported by citation to ICH guidelines in the introduction section.

claim: The risk is better assessed using four key ion currents (IKr, ICaL, INaL, IKs).
source: Yet the risk is better assessed using four key ion currents (IKr, ICaL, INaL, IKs).
evidence: This is supported by the study's methodology and results, as well as citations to previous work.

claim: 100,000 phenotypically diverse cardiomyocytes were simulated to identify the relationship between ion current blockade and ectopic beats.
source: We simulated 100,000 phenotypically diverse cardiomyocytes to identify the underlying relationship between the blockade of those currents and the emergence of ectopic beats in the action potential.
evidence: This describes the computational methodology used in the study.

claim: The axis of arrhythmia serves as a yardstick for quantifying the arrhythmogenic risk of any drug from its profile of multi-channel block alone.
source: It serves as a yardstick for quantifying the arrhythmogenic risk of any drug from its profile of multi-channel block alone.
evidence: This is the main methodological claim of the study, supported by the computational analysis.

claim: The method predicted the clinical risk labels of 109 drugs with an accuracy of 88.1–90.8%.
source: We tested it on 109 drugs and found that it predicted the clinical risk labels with an accuracy of 88.1–90.8%.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the validation study.

claim: Torsades des Pointes is a potentially lethal ventricular arrhythmia that can be induced by many classes of drugs.
source: Torsades des Pointes is a potentially lethal ventricular arrhythmia that can be induced by many classes of drugs. These include antibiotics, antipsychotics, antihistamines, chemotherapeutics, and anti-arrhythmics (Yap and Camm, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Yap and Camm, 2003.

claim: International safety guidelines require hERG block to be assessed in living cells prior to conducting human trials.
source: For this reason, international safety guidelines require hERG block to be assessed in living cells prior to conducting human trials (ICH, 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to ICH, 2005 guidelines.

claim: The standard hERG assay is overly sensitive.
source: However, the standard hERG assay is overly sensitive.
evidence: This is supported by subsequent explanation and citations about multi-channel effects.

claim: The standard hERG assay does not accommodate multi-channel effects which render some drugs safe despite blocking hERG.
source: It does not accommodate multi-channel effects which render some drugs safe despite blocking hERG (Martin et al., 2004; Hoffmann and Warner, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Martin et al., 2004 and Hoffmann and Warner, 2006.

claim: Many useful drugs are prematurely abandoned during pre-clinical trials due to the overly sensitive hERG assay.
source: Consequently, many useful drugs are prematurely abandoned during pre-clinical trials.
evidence: This is an inference based on the limitations of the hERG assay described in the text.

claim: The safety pharmacology community is actively pursuing new in vitro and in silico assays that improve accuracy by targeting multiple ion channels.
source: The safety pharmacology community is actively pursuing new in vitro and in silico assays that improve accuracy by targeting multiple ion channels (Pugsley et al., 2008; Colatsky et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Pugsley et al., 2008 and Colatsky et al., 2016.

claim: In silico assays use computational models of cardiomyocyte electrophysiology in place of a living cell.
source: In silico assays use computational models of cardiomyocyte electrophysiology in place of a living cell (Mirams et al., 2011; Lancaster and Sobie, 2016; Mann et al., 2016; Dutta et al., 2017; Passini et al., 2017; Ballouz et al., 2021; Llopis-Lorente et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations describing in silico methods.

claim: Drug blockade is simulated in the model by attenuating the conductivity of the relevant ion currents.
source: Drug blockade (Figure 1A) is simulated in the model (Figure 1B) by attenuating the conductivity of the relevant ion currents.
evidence: This describes the computational methodology and references Figure 1.

claim: Individual phenotypes are constructed by randomizing the conductance parameters to mimic natural variation in ion channel expression.
source: The individual phenotypes are constructed by randomizing the conductance parameters to mimic natural variation in ion channel expression.
evidence: This describes the methodology for creating phenotypic diversity in the simulations.

claim: The method produces a population of cardiac action potentials.
source: The method produces a population of cardiac action potentials (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 1C showing simulated action potentials.

claim: The action potentials of 100,000 randomized ventricular cardiomyocytes were simulated using a variant of the O'Hara-Rudy model.
source: The action potentials of 100,000 randomized ventricular cardiomyocytes (Figure 2A) were simulated using a variant of the O'Hara-Rudy model (O'Hara et al., 2011) that was optimized for long QT syndrome (Mann et al., 2016; Krogh-Madsen et al., 2017).
evidence: This describes the computational methodology with citations to the model sources.

claim: Early after-depolarizations were chosen as a biomarker for Torsades des Pointes.
source: Early after-depolarizations were chosen as a biomarker for Torsades des Pointes.
evidence: This describes the methodological choice for the study.

claim: Cardiomyocytes that exhibited early after-depolarizations were classified as ectopic.
source: Cardiomyocytes that exhibited early after-depolarizations were classified as ectopic (red) and those that did not were classified as benign (gray).
evidence: This describes the classification methodology used in the study.

claim: The use of the logarithmic coordinate frame is crucial to the subsequent analysis.
source: The use of the logarithmic coordinate frame is crucial to our subsequent analysis.
evidence: This is explained in the context of the mathematical framework developed in the study.

claim: The ectopic and benign phenotypes were clearly segregated in parameter space.
source: The ectopic and benign phenotypes were clearly segregated in parameter space (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: This is demonstrated visually in Figures 2C and 2D.

claim: Multivariate logistic regression was used to identify the linear boundary that best separated the two classes.
source: Multivariate logistic regression was used to identify the linear boundary (dashed line) that best separated the two classes.
evidence: This describes the statistical methodology used in the study.

claim: Drugs attenuate the conductivity of ion channels in a multiplicative fashion.
source: Drugs attenuate the conductivity of ion channels in a multiplicative fashion.
evidence: This is based on established pharmacological knowledge about drug-channel interactions.

claim: Logarithmic coordinates transform the action of drug blockade into an additive process.
source: Logarithmic coordinates transform the action of drug blockade into an additive process
evidence: This is a mathematical property demonstrated in the manuscript.

claim: The axis of arrhythmia runs orthogonally to the decision boundary.
source: We define the axis of arrhythmia as a line that runs orthogonally to the decision boundary (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a mathematical definition central to the method, illustrated in Figure 3A.

claim: The axis of arrhythmia represents the shortest path for shifting any cardiomyocyte into the ectopic regime by modifying the conductances of its ion channels.
source: It represents the shortest path for shifting any cardiomyocyte into the ectopic regime by modifying the conductances of its ion channels.
evidence: This is a mathematical property of orthogonal projection onto the decision boundary.

claim: The arrhythmogenic component of a drug is obtained by projecting the action of the drug onto the axis of arrhythmia.
source: The arrhythmogenic component of a drug is obtained by projecting the action of the drug onto the axis of arrhythmia.
evidence: This describes the mathematical methodology for calculating drug risk.

claim: Drugs that shift the electrophysiology toward the ectopic region have positive risk scores.
source: According to our metric, drugs that shift the electrophysiology toward the ectopic region have positive scores, whereas drugs that shift it away from ectopy have negative scores.
evidence: This describes the interpretation of the risk metric.

claim: Drugs that shift the electrophysiology away from ectopy have negative risk scores.
source: According to our metric, drugs that shift the electrophysiology toward the ectopic region have positive scores, whereas drugs that shift it away from ectopy have negative scores.
evidence: This describes the interpretation of the risk metric.

claim: The proportion of the natural population susceptible to a given drug can be calculated by analyzing how the drug shifts the population density with respect to the decision boundary.
source: We calculated the proportion of the natural population that would be susceptible to a given drug by analyzing how the drug shifts the population density with respect to the decision boundary.
evidence: This describes the methodology for population-level risk assessment.

claim: The natural population in logarithmic parameter space is represented by a symmetric multivariate Gaussian density function.
source: The natural population is therefore represented in logarithmic parameter space by a symmetric multivariate normal distribution.
evidence: This is a mathematical consequence of the log-normal distribution assumption.

claim: The size of the susceptible population is a monotonic function of the drug's risk score.
source: The size of the susceptible population is a monotonic function of the drug's risk score, so the torsadogenic risk can be described using either terminology.
evidence: This is a mathematical property of the model demonstrated in the results.

claim: In the Credible Meds labeling scheme, Class 1 drugs carry a known torsadogenic risk.
source: In that labeling scheme, Class 1 drugs carry a known torsadogenic risk; Class 2 drugs carry a possible risk; Class 3 drugs carry a risk but only in conjunction with other factors; Class 4 drugs have no evidence of risk at all.
evidence: This describes the clinical risk classification system from Credible Meds.

claim: Class 2 drugs carry a possible torsadogenic risk.
source: In that labeling scheme, Class 1 drugs carry a known torsadogenic risk; Class 2 drugs carry a possible risk; Class 3 drugs carry a risk but only in conjunction with other factors; Class 4 drugs have no evidence of risk at all.
evidence: This describes the clinical risk classification system from Credible Meds.

claim: Class 3 drugs carry a torsadogenic risk but only in conjunction with other factors.
source: In that labeling scheme, Class 1 drugs carry a known torsadogenic risk; Class 2 drugs carry a possible risk; Class 3 drugs carry a risk but only in conjunction with other factors; Class 4 drugs have no evidence of risk at all.
evidence: This describes the clinical risk classification system from Credible Meds.

claim: Class 4 drugs have no evidence of torsadogenic risk.
source: In that labeling scheme, Class 1 drugs carry a known torsadogenic risk; Class 2 drugs carry a possible risk; Class 3 drugs carry a risk but only in conjunction with other factors; Class 4 drugs have no evidence of risk at all.
evidence: This describes the clinical risk classification system from Credible Meds.

claim: The signs of the risk scores suggest that Ajmaline is pro-arrhythmic whereas Linezolid is not, which agrees with the clinical risk labels.
source: The signs of the scores suggest that Ajmaline is pro-arrhythmic whereas Linezolid is not, which agrees with the clinical risk labels.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the risk scores in relation to clinical data.

claim: The sizable negative score for Linezolid suggests that it may actually have anti-arrhythmic properties.
source: Indeed, the sizable negative score for Linezolid suggests that it may actually have anti-arrhythmic properties.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the negative risk score.

claim: At 25× dose, Ajmaline shifts the population density by 1.16 units toward the ectopic regime, making 26% of the population susceptible to Torsades.
source: Ajmaline shifts the population density by 1.16 units toward the ectopic regime, making 26% of the population susceptible to Torsades.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the population analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claim: At 25× dose, Linezolid shifts the population 1.18 units away from the ectopic regime, making only 0.0095% of the population susceptible.
source: Conversely, Linezolid shifts the population 1.18 units away from the ectopic regime, making only 0.0095% of the population susceptible, which is a substantial drop compared to the baseline rate of 0.93%.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the population analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The baseline rate of ectopy in the population is 0.93%.
source: Conversely, Linezolid shifts the population 1.18 units away from the ectopic regime, making only 0.0095% of the population susceptible, which is a substantial drop compared to the baseline rate of 0.93%.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the population analysis.

claim: The action of a drug subtly changes direction with dosage because of differing response rates for each ion channel.
source: The action of a drug subtly changes direction with dosage because of differing response rates for each ion channel.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 6 showing curvilinear drug pathways.

claim: The dose-dependent action of drugs follows a gentle arc in parameter space rather than a straight line.
source: Its dose-dependent action thus follows a gentle arc in parameter space rather than a straight line (Figure 6B, left).
evidence: This is demonstrated visually in Figure 6B.

claim: The risk scores depend on dosage due to the curvature of drug pathways in four-dimensional parameter space.
source: That curvature influences how these drugs project onto the axis of arrhythmia, hence the risk scores depend on dosage.
evidence: This is an inference from the mathematical analysis of curvilinear drug pathways.

claim: The shifting risk scores reflect the changing balance of ionic currents that occur naturally with multi-channel drugs.
source: The shifting scores reflect the changing balance of ionic currents that occur naturally with multi-channel drugs.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the dose-dependent risk scores.

claim: The classification accuracy for all dosage levels was found to lay between 88.1% and 90.8%.
source: The classification accuracy for all dosage levels was found to lay between 88.1% and 90.8% (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the validation study shown in Figure 8A.

claim: The conventional hERG assay has an accuracy of 78.9% for the same dataset.
source: In comparison, the conventional hERG assay has an accuracy of 78.9% for the same dataset (Llopis-Lorente et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a comparison to results from Llopis-Lorente et al., 2020.

claim: The area under the ROC curve (AUROC) for drugs at 5× dose is 91.3%.
source: In our case, there is little difference between the ROC curves for drugs assessed at 5× dose versus 25× dose. The areas under the respective ROC curves (AUROC) are nearly identical at 91.3% and 91.5%.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the ROC analysis shown in Figure 8B.

claim: The area under the ROC curve (AUROC) for drugs at 25× dose is 91.5%.
source: In our case, there is little difference between the ROC curves for drugs assessed at 5× dose versus 25× dose. The areas under the respective ROC curves (AUROC) are nearly identical at 91.3% and 91.5%.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the ROC analysis shown in Figure 8C.

claim: The major benefit of the metric is that it can be applied to novel drugs without conducting new computer simulations.
source: The major benefit of the metric is that it can be applied to novel drugs without conducting new computer simulations.
evidence: This is a stated advantage of the proposed method.

claim: The ion currents can be measured using standard patch clamp techniques.
source: The ion currents can be measured using standard patch clamp techniques and the risk metric can be calculated with pen and paper.
evidence: This describes the practical application of the method using established experimental techniques.

claim: The risk metric can be calculated with pen and paper.
source: The ion currents can be measured using standard patch clamp techniques and the risk metric can be calculated with pen and paper.
evidence: This emphasizes the simplicity of the calculation once the axis is established.

claim: All of the simulations in the present study were conducted in the absence of drugs.
source: All of the simulations in the present study were conducted in the absence of drugs.
evidence: This describes a key methodological feature of the study.

claim: The simulations were only needed to identify the axis of arrhythmia and do not need to be repeated when applying the metric.
source: The simulations were only needed to identify the axis of arrhythmia and do not need to be repeated when applying the metric.
evidence: This describes the one-time nature of the computational work.

claim: The axis encapsulates the principal relationship between ion channel blockade and the onset of early after-depolarizations.
source: The axis encapsulates the principal relationship between ion channel blockade and the onset of early after-depolarizations.
evidence: This describes the biological meaning of the axis of arrhythmia.

claim: The axis represents the most potent combination of pro-arrhythmic block that is theoretically possible for any drug, averaged across all cardiomyocytes.
source: It represents the most potent combination of pro-arrhythmic block that is theoretically possible for any drug, averaged across all cardiomyocytes.
evidence: This describes the theoretical interpretation of the axis.

claim: The assumption that the boundary is linear is crucial for generalizing the findings across all cardiomyocytes.
source: The assumption that the boundary is linear is crucial for generalizing the findings across all cardiomyocytes.
evidence: This explains a key methodological choice in the study.

claim: A linear boundary allows the effect of a drug to be analyzed independently of the individual cardiomyocytes.
source: It allows the effect of a drug to be analyzed independently of the individual cardiomyocytes.
evidence: This explains the advantage of the linear boundary assumption.

claim: Drug blockade and phenotypic diversity both operate on the same properties of ion channels.
source: The analysis is possible because drug blockade and phenotypic diversity both operate on the same properties of ion channels.
evidence: This explains why the method can predict population effects without explicit simulation.

claim: The two biological processes (drug blockade and phenotypic diversity) are mathematically interchangeable.
source: The two biological processes are therefore mathematically interchangeable.
evidence: This is a mathematical insight that enables the population analysis.

claim: The distribution of the drugged population can be inferred from the drug-free population by shifting it according to the drug's risk score.
source: As such, the distribution of the drugged population can be inferred from the drug-free population by shifting it according to the drug's risk score.
evidence: This describes the mathematical method for population-level prediction.

claim: The CiPA steering committee recommends that the electrophysiology be simulated using the CiPAORdv1.0 variant of the O'Hara-Rudy model.
source: The CiPA steering committee (Li et al., 2019) recommends that the electrophysiology be simulated using the CiPAORdv1.0 variant of the O'Hara-Rudy model which incorporates the kinetics of drugs binding with the hERG channel (Li et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Li et al., 2019 and Li et al., 2017.

claim: Low versus intermediate-or-high risk CiPA drugs were predicted with 84–95% accuracy using manual patch clamp techniques.
source: Low versus intermediate-or-high risk drugs were predicted with 84–95% accuracy using manual patch clamp techniques; or 93–100% accuracy using automated patch clamping (Li et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a comparison to results from Li et al., 2019.

claim: Low versus intermediate-or-high risk CiPA drugs were predicted with 93–100% accuracy using automated patch clamping.
source: Low versus intermediate-or-high risk drugs were predicted with 84–95% accuracy using manual patch clamp techniques; or 93–100% accuracy using automated patch clamping (Li et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a comparison to results from Li et al., 2019.

claim: Passini et al., 2017, used a larger dataset (n=62) to obtain 89% accuracy at predicting Class 1 versus Class 2–4 torsadogenic risk labels from Credible Meds.
source: Passini et al., 2017, used a larger dataset (n=62) to obtain 89% accuracy at predicting Class 1 versus Class 2–4 torsadogenic risk labels from Credible Meds.
evidence: This is a comparison to results from Passini et al., 2017.

claim: Llopis-Lorente et al., 2020, found that qNet predicted Class 1–2 versus Class 3–4 torsadogenic risk with 92.7% accuracy.
source: Their best performing biomarker was qNet, which predicted Class 1–2 versus Class 3–4 torsadogenic risk with 92.7% accuracy.
evidence: This is a comparison to results from Llopis-Lorente et al., 2020.

claim: Llopis-Lorente et al., 2020, increased the overall performance to 94.5% by combining the best biomarkers into a decision tree.
source: Llopis-Lorente et al., 2020, increased the overall performance to 94.5% by combining the best biomarkers into a decision tree.
evidence: This is a comparison to results from Llopis-Lorente et al., 2020.

claim: Early after-depolarizations proved to be the worst biomarker in the Llopis-Lorente et al., 2020 study, with only 78.9% accuracy.
source: Interestingly, early after-depolarizations proved to be their worst biomarker, with only 78.9% accuracy, which is quite different to our findings.
evidence: This is a comparison to results from Llopis-Lorente et al., 2020.

claim: The Llopis-Lorente et al., 2020 method under-estimated the predictive power of early after-depolarizations by only exploring normal physiological limits where such events are rare.
source: We suspect that their method under-estimated the predictive power of early after-depolarizations by only exploring normal physiological limits where such events are rare.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the difference in results.

claim: Kramer et al., 2013, trained six candidate MICE models on a dataset of 55 drugs.
source: Kramer et al., 2013, trained six candidate models on a dataset of 55 drugs.
evidence: This is a description of the MICE model study from Kramer et al., 2013.

claim: The best MICE model predicted the clinical risk labels of drugs with 90.9% accuracy using only the difference between hERG and Cav1.2.
source: Their best model predicted the clinical risk labels of the drugs with 90.9% accuracy using only the difference between hERG and Cav1.2.
evidence: This is a comparison to results from Kramer et al., 2013.

claim: The accuracy of the MICE model and the current model is nearly identical, albeit on different datasets.
source: Interestingly, the accuracy of the two models is nearly identical, albeit on different datasets.
evidence: This is a comparison of performance between the two approaches.

claim: Bnet predicts the torsadogenic risk of a drug directly from the net blockade of inward and outward ion currents.
source: Bnet (Mistry, 2018) is a simple linear model that predicts the torsadogenic risk of a drug directly from the net blockade of inward and outward ion currents.
evidence: This describes the Bnet model with citation to Mistry, 2018.

claim: Bnet predicts the clinical risk labels of the CiPA validation drugs as accurately as the CiPAORdv1.0 model when adjusted for drug binding kinetics.
source: Bnet predicts the clinical risk labels of the CiPA validation drugs as accurately as the CiPAORdv1.0 model when adjusted for drug binding kinetics (Li et al., 2019; Mistry, 2019; Han et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Li et al., 2019, Mistry, 2019, and Han et al., 2019.

claim: The current approach resolves the debate between model complexity and biophysical realism by combining both approaches into the same enterprise.
source: Our approach resolves the debate between model complexity and biophysical realism by combining both approaches into the same enterprise.
evidence: This is a claim about the methodological contribution of the study.

claim: Complex biophysical models were used to identify the relationship between ion channels and torsadogenic risk as it is best understood by theory.
source: Complex biophysical models were used to identify the relationship between ion channels and torsadogenic risk — as it is best understood by theory.
evidence: This describes the first step of the methodological approach.

claim: The findings were reduced to a simpler linear model that can be applied to novel drugs without recapitulating the complex computer simulations.
source: Those findings were then reduced to a simpler linear model that can be applied to novel drugs without recapitulating the complex computer simulations.
evidence: This describes the second step of the methodological approach.

claim: The reduced model retains a biophysical description of multi-channel drug block, but only as far as necessary to predict the likelihood of early after-depolarizations.
source: The reduced model retains a biophysical description of multi-channel drug block, but only as far as necessary to predict the likelihood of early after-depolarizations.
evidence: This describes the balance achieved in the methodological approach.

claim: The reduced model does not reproduce the action potential itself.
source: It does not reproduce the action potential itself.
evidence: This describes a limitation of the reduced model.

claim: The benefits of this approach will accelerate the adoption of computational assays in safety pharmacology and ultimately reduce the burden of animal testing.
source: We believe the benefits of this approach will accelerate the adoption of computational assays in safety pharmacology and ultimately reduce the burden of animal testing.
evidence: This is a speculative claim about the potential impact of the method.

claim: The dataset of drugs was drawn from multiple sources and diverse experimental conditions.
source: The method was evaluated using a dataset of drugs that were drawn from multiple sources and diverse experimental conditions (Llopis-Lorente et al., 2020).
evidence: This describes a limitation of the validation dataset.

claim: Drug potency measurements differ prominently between laboratories and recording platforms.
source: It is known that such measurements differ prominently between laboratories and recording platforms (Kramer et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kramer et al., 2020.

claim: The accuracy of the predictions is limited by the quality of the drug potency measurements.
source: The accuracy of the predictions is therefore limited by the quality of the drug potency measurements.
evidence: This is an inference about a limitation of the method.

claim: The accuracy of the axis of arrhythmia is limited by the quality of the biophysical model from which it is derived.
source: The accuracy of the axis of arrhythmia is likewise limited by the quality of the biophysical model from which it is derived.
evidence: This is an inference about a limitation of the method.

claim: The present study only investigated one particular variant of the ORd model paced at 1 Hz.
source: The present study only investigated one particular variant of the ORd model (O'Hara et al., 2011; Krogh-Madsen et al., 2017) paced at 1 Hz.
evidence: This describes a limitation of the study scope.

claim: Other models and pacing rates are likely to produce differing estimates of the axis.
source: Other models and pacing rates are likely to produce differing estimates of the axis.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential variations in results.

claim: The model was paced at 1 Hz with a stimulus of –70 mV and duration of 0.5 ms.
source: The model was paced at 1 Hz with a stimulus of –70 mV and duration of 0.5 ms.
evidence: This describes the simulation parameters used in the study.

claim: All simulations were equilibrated for at least 1000 beats prior to analysis.
source: All simulations were equilibrated for at least 1000 beats prior to analysis.
evidence: This describes the simulation methodology.

claim: Cells were classified as ectopic if any of four successive beats contained an early after-depolarization defined by any secondary peak that rose above –50 mV and was separated from other peaks by at least 100 ms.
source: Cells were classified as ectopic if any of those four beats contained an early after-depolarization — as defined by any secondary peak that rose above –50 mV and was separated from other peaks by at least 100 ms.
evidence: This describes the classification criteria used in the study.

claim: The parameter domain is large enough to cover the ectopic region, but not so large as to be unduly influenced by biological extremes.
source: That domain is large enough to cover the ectopic region, but not so large as to be unduly influenced by biological extremes.
evidence: This explains the rationale for the parameter domain choice.

claim: The parameters span between 0.05 and 20 times their baseline value.
source: The parameters span between 0.05 and 20 times their baseline value.
evidence: This describes the range of parameter variation.

claim: The spread of the log-normal distribution was based on experience with previous simulations.
source: The spread was based on our experience with previous simulations (Sadrieh et al., 2013; Sadrieh et al., 2014; Ballouz et al., 2021; TeBay et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The ion channel species were assumed to vary independently.
source: The ion channel species were assumed to vary independently.
evidence: This describes a modeling assumption.
